title: Unsigned prefix deletion bijection for stable Cech sorting
statement:
Let $I$ be a linearly ordered type, $p\ge0$, $n=p+2$, and $t:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to I$.
Use stable sorting and partial sorting [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators].
Let $O_t$ be the set of quadruples $(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$ with
$\sigma,\tau\in S_n$, $a\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)$,
$\operatorname{cechStableSort}(t,\sigma)$, $\operatorname{cechPartialSort}(\sigma,\tau,a)$,
$r<a$.
Let $N_t$ be the set of quadruples $(j,\rho,b,\eta)$ with
$j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $\rho,\eta\in S_{n-1}$, $b\in\operatorname{Fin}(n-1)$,
$\operatorname{cechStableSort}(t\circ\delta_j,\rho)$,
$\operatorname{cechPartialSort}(\rho,\eta,b)$, and
$t(j)<t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ or $t(j)=t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ and $j<\delta_j(\rho(b))$.
Here $S_m$ is the permutation group of $\operatorname{Fin}(m)$ and $\delta_j$ is the increasing map omitting $j$.
There exists an equivalence $e:O_t\simeq N_t$ such that if $e(\sigma,a,\tau,r)=(j,\rho,b,\eta)$,
then $a=b+1$, $r<n$, $\tau(r)=j$, and for every $k\in\operatorname{Fin}(n-1)$,
$\sigma(\delta_r(k))=\delta_j(\rho(k))$ and $\tau(\delta_r(k))=\delta_j(\eta(k))$.
In these restriction identities $r$ is regarded as an element of $\operatorname{Fin}(n)$.

proof.text: Use stable sorting and partial sorting from [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. For an outgoing quadruple $(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$, $r<a$ implies $r<n$. The partial-sort prefix gives $j=\tau(r)=\sigma(r)$. Delete position $r$ and label $j$ from both permutations and renumber the remaining labels increasingly through $\delta_j$. Put $b=a-1$. The restricted stable permutation orders exactly the remaining pairs $(t(k),k)$, because $\delta_j$ is increasing and thus preserves tie breaking. Agreement of the prefixes persists before $b$, and increasing tails persist starting at $b$. The omitted label precedes the remaining stable junction since its original stable rank was $r<a$. This constructs an incoming quadruple and gives both restriction identities and $a=b+1$.

Conversely, take an incoming $(j,\rho,b,\eta)$. Let $r$ be the number of remaining labels $k$ whose pair $(t(k),k)$ is less than $(t(j),j)$. The before condition implies $r\le b$. Insert $j$ at position $r$ into the lists $\delta_j\circ\rho$ and $\delta_j\circ\eta$, and put $a=b+1$. The first permutation is stably sorted, and the second agrees with it on the first $a$ positions; its tail starting at $a$ remains increasing. Deletion and insertion are inverse: the stable rank uniquely recovers $r$, $a=b+1$ recovers the prefix length, and the increasing renumbering recovers both permutations. Thus the two maps define an equivalence. This works for $b=0$, $b=n-2$, constant tuples, and all repeated values; an empty ordered type has no input tuple.

lean.statement:
theorem cechPrefixDeletionBijection {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : CechPrefixOutgoing p t ≃ CechPrefixIncoming p t, ∀ x,
      let y := e x
      x.1.2.1.val = y.1.2.2.1.val + 1 ∧
      ∃ hr : x.1.2.2.2.val < p + 2,
        x.1.2.2.1 ⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ = y.1.1 ∧
        (∀ k : Fin (p + 1),
          x.1.1 ((⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ : Fin (p + 2)).succAbove k) =
            y.1.1.succAbove (y.1.2.1 k)) ∧
        (∀ k : Fin (p + 1),
          x.1.2.2.1 ((⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ : Fin (p + 2)).succAbove k) =
            y.1.1.succAbove (y.1.2.2.2 k))
